newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok wants to keep the flags flying for Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok wants to keep the flags flying for Clinton.

text.p: City officials have opted for a rush job in an attempt to to outwit flag thieves ahead of U.S. President Bill Clinton's arrival in Bangkok late on Monday.

Over the weekend workers began setting set up American and Thai flags along the route Clinton will travel during his 27-hour visit to Thailand, but they found that dozens had been stolen just hours later.
So they stopped work and decided to do a blitz on Monday before Clinton arrives at around 9:30 p.m. (1430 GMT) in a bid to foil light-fingered collectors.
"We decided to erect the U.S. flags on Monday morning and officials will stand watch to prevent them from being stolen," City Clerk Prasert Samalapa told reporters.

City officials are also rushing to remove thousands of "krathong" from waterways throughout Bangkok. Sunday night was the annual "Loy Krathong" festival when Thais launch the small boats made of banana and lotus leaves into lakes, canals and rivers for good luck.
Normally the Krathongs, laden with offerings, money and candles, litter the waterways for days. But officials have ordered round-the-clock clean-up efforts.

Security is also tight ahead of Clinton's visit -- the first to Thailand by an American president in 27 years -- as police and military assisted by an army of U.S. security personnel will conduct random checks along the route Clinton will travel.
"But for us we are more concerned about the U.S. flags and the cleaniness of the city than the security aspect," a city official said.
Giant paintings of Bangkok's historical landmarks and portraits of the U.S. president and first lady have been erected on billboards around the city to welcome the couple.
So far 175 people, mostly illegal immigrants from India, Burma, Pakistan and Bangladesh, have been arrested and detained by immigration authorities.
"Even though we don't have criminal records for these people we have to detain them just in case," a police officer said.
